+// The template-structure contract (runtime/cli/utils/template-structure.js,
+// loadTemplateContract) marks a template section optional when its H2 header
+// carries one of these prefixes and required otherwise. This is its twin, and a
+// parity test pins the two required sets together.
+const OPTIONAL_TEMPLATE_HEADER_RE = /^(?:L(?:2|3\+?)|FIX ADDENDUM)\s*:/iu;
+const TEMPLATE_ANCHOR_OPEN_LINE_RE = /<!--\s*ANCHOR:([A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]*)\s*-->/u;
+const TEMPLATE_ANCHOR_CLOSE_LINE_RE = /<!--\s*\/ANCHOR:([A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]*)\s*-->/u;
+
+function templateH2Headers(content: string): string[] {
+  return [...stripFences(content).matchAll(/^##\s+(.+)$/gmu)].map((match) => match[1].trim());
+}
+
+function normalizeTemplateHeader(header: string): string {
+  return header.replace(/\[[^\]]+\]/gu, '').replace(/^\d+\.\s*/u, '').replace(/\s+/gu, ' ').trim().toUpperCase();
+}
+
+// Each anchor the doc's rendered template requires, with the H2 heading of its
+// section so a missing one can be named and restored in one pass.
+function requiredTemplateSections(level: SpecKitLevel, docName: string): Array<{ id: string; heading: string }> {
+  // The decision record's sections are per ADR and named by the author, so its
+  // template fixes no required anchor.
+  if (path.basename(docName) === 'decision-record.md') return [];
+  const template = renderedTemplate(level, docName);
+  if (template === null) return [];
+  const headers = templateH2Headers(template);
+  const required = new Set(headers.filter((header) => !OPTIONAL_TEMPLATE_HEADER_RE.test(header)).map(normalizeTemplateHeader));
+  const optional = new Set(headers.filter((header) => OPTIONAL_TEMPLATE_HEADER_RE.test(header)).map(normalizeTemplateHeader));
+  const lines = template.split(/\r?\n/u);
+  const seen = new Set<string>();
+  const sections: Array<{ id: string; heading: string }> = [];
+  for (let index = 0; index < lines.length; index += 1) {
+    const open = lines[index].match(TEMPLATE_ANCHOR_OPEN_LINE_RE);
+    if (!open) continue;
+    const id = open[1];
+    let end = -1;
+    for (let inner = index + 1; inner < lines.length; inner += 1) {
+      const close = lines[inner].match(TEMPLATE_ANCHOR_CLOSE_LINE_RE);
+      if (close && close[1] === id) {
+        end = inner;
+        break;
+      }
+    }
+    if (end === -1) continue;
+    const sectionHeaders = templateH2Headers(lines.slice(index, end + 1).join('\n'));
+    const requiredHeading = sectionHeaders.find((header) => required.has(normalizeTemplateHeader(header)));
+    const hasOptional = sectionHeaders.some((header) => optional.has(normalizeTemplateHeader(header)));
+    if ((requiredHeading !== undefined || hasOptional) && !seen.has(id)) {
+      seen.add(id);
+      if (requiredHeading !== undefined) sections.push({ id, heading: requiredHeading });
+    }
+    index = end;
+  }
+  return sections;
+}
+
+function requiredTemplateAnchors(level: SpecKitLevel, docName: string): string[] {
+  return requiredTemplateSections(level, docName).map((section) => section.id);
+}

+# Succeeds when the doc carries a SPECKIT_TEMPLATE_SOURCE stamp of v2.3 or later
+# within its first 70 lines. The checks added with that template version apply
+# only to such docs, so a doc with an older stamp, or none, keeps its verdict.
+speckit_carries_token_gate_stamp() {
+    local filepath="$1"
+    local stamp_line major minor
+    stamp_line=$(head -n 70 "$filepath" 2>/dev/null | \
+        grep -m1 -E '^[[:space:]]*<!--[[:space:]]*SPECKIT_TEMPLATE_SOURCE:[^|>]*\|[[:space:]]*v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+[[:space:]]*-->' || true)
+    [[ -n "$stamp_line" ]] || return 1
+    major=$(printf '%s' "$stamp_line" | sed -E 's/.*\|[[:space:]]*v([0-9]+)\.([0-9]+).*/\1/')
+    minor=$(printf '%s' "$stamp_line" | sed -E 's/.*\|[[:space:]]*v([0-9]+)\.([0-9]+).*/\2/')
+    if (( major > 2 )) || { (( major == 2 )) && (( minor >= 3 )); }; then
+        return 0
+    fi
+    return 1
+}

+// ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+// MODULE: Create.sh Track Containment

+import fs from 'node:fs';
+import os from 'node:os';
+import path from 'node:path';
+import { execFileSync, spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
+import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
+
+const CLI_DIR = path.resolve(__dirname, '..');
+const SKILL_ROOT = path.resolve(CLI_DIR, '../..');
+
+// A track names a folder under specs/. The value comes from whoever runs the
+// scaffold, often a model filling in a command template, so a value that
+// climbs out of specs/ must be refused before anything is written. The
+// sandbox repository sits one level inside its temp folder, so an escape of
+// two levels still lands inside the temp folder and the test can see it.
+let sandbox: string;
+let workspace: string;
+let createScript: string;
+
+beforeEach(() => {
+  sandbox = fs.realpathSync(fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'create-track-containment-')));
+  workspace = path.join(sandbox, 'repo');
+  fs.mkdirSync(workspace);
+  execFileSync('git', ['init', '--quiet'], { cwd: workspace });
+  const fixtureCli = path.join(workspace, '.skilled', 'skills', 'system-spec-kit', 'runtime', 'cli');
+  for (const dir of ['spec', 'lib', 'templates']) {
+    fs.mkdirSync(path.join(fixtureCli, dir), { recursive: true });
+  }
+  for (const script of ['create.sh', 'refresh-track-roots.mjs']) {
+    fs.copyFileSync(path.join(CLI_DIR, 'spec', script), path.join(fixtureCli, 'spec', script));
+  }
+  for (const library of ['shell-common.sh', 'git-branch.sh', 'template-utils.sh', 'track-roots.mjs']) {
+    fs.copyFileSync(path.join(CLI_DIR, 'lib', library), path.join(fixtureCli, 'lib', library));
+  }
+  fs.copyFileSync(
+    path.join(CLI_DIR, 'templates', 'inline-gate-renderer.sh'),
+    path.join(fixtureCli, 'templates', 'inline-gate-renderer.sh'),
+  );
+  fs.cpSync(
+    path.join(SKILL_ROOT, 'templates'),
+    path.join(workspace, '.skilled', 'skills', 'system-spec-kit', 'templates'),
+    { recursive: true },
+  );
+  createScript = path.join(fixtureCli, 'spec', 'create.sh');
+});
+
+afterEach(() => {
+  fs.rmSync(sandbox, { recursive: true, force: true });
+});
+
+function create(track: string) {
+  return spawnSync(
+    'bash',
+    [createScript, '--json', '--skip-branch', '--track', track, '--short-name', 'probe', 'Probe packet'],
+    { cwd: workspace, encoding: 'utf8' },
+  );
+}
+
+// Every path in the sandbox except git's own bookkeeping, so a refused run can
+// be shown to have written nothing anywhere.
+function listing(): string[] {
+  const out: string[] = [];
+  const walk = (dir: string) => {
+    for (const entry of fs.readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true })) {
+      if (entry.name === '.git' || entry.name === '.skilled') continue;
+      const full = path.join(dir, entry.name);
+      out.push(path.relative(sandbox, full));
+      if (entry.isDirectory()) walk(full);
+    }
+  };
+  walk(sandbox);
+  return out.sort();
+}

+      expect(result.stderr).toContain('--track');

+    });

+  });
+

+// ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+// MODULE: Post-Edit Placeholder Scan
+// ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
+import fs from 'node:fs';
+import os from 'node:os';
+import path from 'node:path';
+import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
+
+import { afterEach, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
+
+// The post-edit hook runs this scan on the folder of every spec doc an author
+// edits and shows a failure as a warning. It is useful only while it reports
+// what strict validation would flag: a marker strict validation reads must be
+// counted, and bracketed prose strict validation ignores must not be.
+const here = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
+const cliRoot = path.resolve(here, '..');
+const scanScript = path.join(cliRoot, 'spec', 'check-placeholders.sh');
+const fixturesRoot = path.join(cliRoot, 'test-fixtures');
+const createdRoots = new Set<string>();
+
+const V23_STAMP = '<!-- SPECKIT_TEMPLATE_SOURCE: spec-core | v2.3 -->';
+const V22_STAMP = '<!-- SPECKIT_TEMPLATE_SOURCE: spec-core | v2.2 -->';
+
+function folderWith(lines: string[]): string {
+  const root = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'post-edit-placeholder-scan-'));
+  createdRoots.add(root);
+  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(root, 'spec.md'), `${lines.join('\n')}\n`, 'utf8');
+  return root;
+}
+
+function scan(folder: string): { count: number; status: string; exit: number | null } {
+  const result = spawnSync('bash', [scanScript, folder, '--json'], { encoding: 'utf8' });
+  const report = JSON.parse(result.stdout) as { status: string; placeholders: number; folder: string };
+  return { count: report.placeholders, status: report.status, exit: result.status };
+}
+
+afterEach(() => {
+  for (const root of createdRoots) fs.rmSync(root, { recursive: true, force: true });
+  createdRoots.clear();
+});
+
+describe('post-edit placeholder scan', () => {
+  it('counts the v2.3 value token with its colon', () => {
+    const result = scan(folderWith(['# Spec', '', 'Owner: [YOUR_VALUE_HERE: owner name]']));
+    expect(result).toEqual({ count: 1, status: 'FAIL', exit: 1 });
+  });
+
+  it('counts the other markers strict validation reads', () => {
+    const result = scan(folderWith([
+      '# Spec',
+      'Owner: <YOUR_VALUE_HERE: owner name>',
+      'Scope: [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: which module?]',
+      'Target: [NEEDS_CLARIFICATION: which release?]',
+    ]));
+    expect(result.count).toBe(3);
+  });
+
+  it('ignores bracketed prose that strict validation never flags', () => {
+    const result = scan(folderWith(['# Spec', '', 'Owner: [Owner name]', 'Target: [Response time target]']));
+    expect(result).toEqual({ count: 0, status: 'PASS', exit: 0 });
+  });
+
+  it('passes a template-compliant Level 3 packet', () => {
+    expect(scan(path.join(fixturesRoot, '063-template-compliant-level3')).count).toBe(0);
+  });
+
+  it('reads a v2.3 doc with the code-span, fence and all-markers rules', () => {
+    const result = scan(folderWith([
+      V23_STAMP,
+      'Example `[YOUR_VALUE_HERE: example]` then Owner: [YOUR_VALUE_HERE: owner name]',
+      'Run `create.sh --owner [YOUR_VALUE_HERE: owner name] --force` first',
+      '~~~text',
+      'Owner: [YOUR_VALUE_HERE: owner name]',
+      '~~~',
+      '   ```text',
+      'Owner: [YOUR_VALUE_HERE: owner name]',
+      '   ```',
+    ]));
+    expect(result.count).toBe(1);
+  });
+
+  it('reads an older doc the way strict validation always has', () => {
+    const result = scan(folderWith([
+      V22_STAMP,
+      'Example `[YOUR_VALUE_HERE: example]` then Owner: [YOUR_VALUE_HERE: owner name]',
+      '~~~text',
+      'Owner: [YOUR_VALUE_HERE: owner name]',
+      '~~~',
+    ]));
+    expect(result.count).toBe(1);
+  });
+
+  it('keeps its usage exit code for a missing folder', () => {
+    const result = spawnSync('bash', [scanScript, path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'no-such-placeholder-folder'), '--json'], { encoding: 'utf8' });
+    expect(result.status).toBe(2);
+  });
+});

+  });

+  const found = report.entries.filter((item) => item.rule === 'ANCHORS_VALID');
+  if (found.length !== 1) throw new Error(`expected one ANCHORS_VALID entry, found ${found.length}`);
+  return found[0];

+// A model copies the GOOD example and avoids the WEAK one, so a note without both
+// leaves the section's target to guesswork.
+function fillNoteProblems(note: string): string[] {
+  const inner = note.slice('<!-- FILL: '.length, -' -->'.length);
+  const problems: string[] = [];
+  if (inner.includes('[YOUR_VALUE_HERE:')) problems.push('holds a token');
+  if (inner.includes('[NEEDS')) problems.push('holds a clarification marker');
+  if (inner.includes('-->')) problems.push('holds a comment end');
+  if (!inner.trim().endsWith('.')) problems.push('does not end with a period');
+  if (!/GOOD: .+ WEAK: .+/u.test(inner)) problems.push('lacks a GOOD and then a WEAK example');
+  return problems;
+}

 4. **Error findings make the rule fail:** a checked document with no anchors (`no anchors found`), an anchor opened twice (`duplicate anchor '<name>'`), an anchor that is never closed (`is never closed`), a close with no matching open (`is closed but never opened`), and a close count that exceeds the open count (`is closed more times than it is opened`).

    55	## 2. PROBLEM & PURPOSE
    56	
    57	### Problem Statement
    58	The v4.0.0.11 release shipped the `/doctor:git setup` command and its hardening across code, a command router, skill docs, playbooks, catalogs, changelogs and cross-repo indexes. Nobody has yet checked each of those artifacts against its own sk-doc authoring mode or the sk-code-skilled standards, or confirmed that every repo surface listing doctor commands and `/doctor:git` targets names `setup` correctly.
    59	
    60	### Purpose
    61	A two-lineage deep review (cli-codex gpt-6-luna and cli-pi deepseek-v4.1-flash, five iterations each) produces a review report with path:line findings on standards conformance, correctness, traceability and maintainability for every file listed in `goal-file-manifest.txt`.

    30	# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    31	# 1. HELPERS
    32	# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    33	
    34	# Prints one "line<TAB>kind" row for each line holding an unfilled marker, read
    35	# the way the runtime orchestrator reads it. kind is "token" when every marker
    36	# on the line is a [YOUR_VALUE_HERE: value token, "marker" when any other marker
    37	# is present, and "title" for a [template: token left in a title line.
    38	# Mode "v23", for a doc stamped v2.3 or later, skips fences opened by ``` or ~~~
    39	# at any indent and inline code spans, reads every marker on a line and checks
    40	# the title. Any other mode reads only the first marker on a line, skips it when
    41	# a backtick sits right before it, and knows only ``` fences.
    42	placeholder_marker_lines() {
    43	    local filepath="$1"
    44	    local mode="$2"
    45	    awk -v mode="$mode" '
    46	        function blank_code_spans(s,    out, i, n, j, run, k, m, close_at, end_at, pad) {
    47	            out = ""; i = 1; n = length(s)
    48	            while (i <= n) {
    49	                if (substr(s, i, 1) != "`") { out = out substr(s, i, 1); i++; continue }
    50	                j = i
    51	                while (j <= n && substr(s, j, 1) == "`") j++
    52	                run = j - i
    53	                close_at = 0
    54	                k = j
    55	                while (k <= n) {
    56	                    if (substr(s, k, 1) != "`") { k++; continue }
    57	                    m = k
    58	                    while (m <= n && substr(s, m, 1) == "`") m++
    59	                    if (m - k == run) { close_at = k; break }
    60	                    k = m
    61	                }
    62	                if (!close_at) { out = out substr(s, i, run); i = j; continue }
    63	                end_at = close_at + run
    64	                pad = ""
    65	                for (k = i; k < end_at; k++) pad = pad " "
    66	                out = out pad
    67	                i = end_at
    68	            }
    69	            return out
    70	        }
    71	        BEGIN { in_code = 0; marker = "<YOUR_VALUE_HERE:|\\[YOUR_VALUE_HERE:|\\[NEEDS[_ ]CLARIFICATION:" }
    72	        {
    73	            if (mode == "v23") {
    74	                if ($0 ~ /^[ \t]*(```|~~~)/) { in_code = !in_code; next }
    75	            } else if ($0 ~ /^[ \t]*```/) { in_code = !in_code; next }
    76	            if (in_code) next
    77	            if (mode == "v23") {
    78	                rest = blank_code_spans($0)
    79	                if (rest ~ /^[ \t]*title:.*\[template:/) print NR "\ttitle"
    80	                found = 0
    81	                hard = 0
    82	                while (match(rest, marker)) {
    83	                    found = 1
    84	                    if (substr(rest, RSTART, RLENGTH) != "[YOUR_VALUE_HERE:") hard = 1
    85	                    rest = substr(rest, RSTART + RLENGTH)
    86	                }
    87	                if (found) print NR "\t" (hard ? "marker" : "token")
    88	            } else if (match($0, marker)) {
    89	                if (RSTART > 1 && substr($0, RSTART - 1, 1) == "`") next
    90	                print NR "\tmarker"
    91	            }
    92	        }
    93	    ' "$filepath" 2>/dev/null || true
    94	}

   101	    [[ "$(speckit_status_trim "$value")" == "draft" ]]
   102	}

   768	// Reports whether spec.md's Status is exactly Draft. Mirrors the shell classifier:
   769	// quotes, case, trailing punctuation and repeated spaces do not change the
   770	// answer, any other word does. An older spec is read by its first Status row. A
   771	// v2.3 spec may carry more than one metadata table, and a Complete row in any of
   772	// them is a completion claim, so that row is the one read.
   773	function specStatusIsDraft(folder: string): boolean {
   774	  const spec = readIfExists(path.join(folder, 'spec.md'));
   775	  if (!spec) return false;
   776	  const values: string[] = [];
   777	  for (const line of spec.split(/\r?\n/u)) {
   778	    if (!/^\s*\|/u.test(line)) continue;
   779	    const cells = line.split('|');
   780	    if (cells.length < 3) continue;
   781	    if (cleanStatusCell(cells[1]).toLowerCase() !== 'status') continue;
   782	    values.push(normalizeStatusValue(cells[2]));
   783	  }
   784	  if (values.length === 0) return false;
   785	  const value = carriesTokenGateStamp(spec) ? (values.find(statusIsComplete) ?? values[0]) : values[0];
   786	  return value === 'draft';
   787	}

   789	// The orchestrator's reading of a v2.3 doc line: the markers outside inline code
   790	// spans, and whether a template's [template: provenance token survives in a
   791	// title. Both implementations of the rule read a v2.3 doc this way.
   792	const PLACEHOLDER_MARKERS_ALL_RE = /<YOUR_VALUE_HERE:|\[YOUR_VALUE_HERE:|\[NEEDS_CLARIFICATION:|\[NEEDS CLARIFICATION:/gu;
   793	const TEMPLATE_TITLE_RE = /^\s*title:.*\[template:/u;
   794	const TOKEN_GATE_FENCE_RE = /^\s*(```|~~~)/u;

   796	function validatePlaceholders(folder: string, level: SpecKitLevel): ValidationEntry {
   797	  const findings: string[] = [];
   798	  const draftTokens: string[] = [];
   799	  const draftPacket = specStatusIsDraft(folder);
   800	  // A workflow loop owns the freeform docs and rewrites them whole at
   801	  // synthesis, so a scaffolded skeleton's markers are not an author's debt.
   802	  for (const docName of validationDocsForLevel(folder, level).filter((docName) => !FREEFORM_WORKFLOW_DOCS.has(docName))) {
   803	    const content = readIfExists(path.join(folder, docName));
   804	    if (!content) continue;
   805	    const tokenGated = carriesTokenGateStamp(content);
   806	    const lines = content.split(/\r?\n/u);
   807	    // Track fenced code blocks: a line starting with ``` toggles in_code and is
   808	    // itself skipped, matching check-placeholders.sh awk behavior.
   809	    let inCode = false;
   810	    lines.forEach((line, index) => {
   811	      if (tokenGated) {
   812	        // A v2.3 doc: a fence opens with ``` or ~~~ at any indent, a marker in
   813	        // inline code is an example, and every marker on the line counts.
   814	        if (TOKEN_GATE_FENCE_RE.test(line)) {
   815	          inCode = !inCode;
   816	          return;
   817	        }
   818	        if (inCode) return;
   819	        const visible = stripInlineCode(line);
   820	        const markers = [...visible.matchAll(PLACEHOLDER_MARKERS_ALL_RE)].map((found) => found[0]);
   821	        const title = TEMPLATE_TITLE_RE.test(visible);
   822	        if (markers.length === 0 && !title) return;
   823	        const finding = `${docName}:${index + 1}: ${line.trim().slice(0, 120)}`;
   824	        if (!title && draftPacket && markers.every((marker) => marker === '[YOUR_VALUE_HERE:')) {
   825	          draftTokens.push(finding);
   826	        } else {
   827	          findings.push(finding);
   828	        }
   829	        return;
   830	      }
   831	      if (/^\s*```/u.test(line)) {
   832	        inCode = !inCode;
   833	        return;
   834	      }
   835	      if (inCode) return;
   836	      const match = PLACEHOLDER_MARKER_RE.exec(line);
   837	      if (!match) return;
   838	      // Skip inline-backtick-wrapped markers: if the matched marker is
   839	      // immediately preceded by a backtick on this line, it is escaped content
   840	      // (parity with the shell rule's grep -v of backtick-wrapped cases).
   841	      if (match.index > 0 && line.charAt(match.index - 1) === '`') return;
   842	      const finding = `${docName}:${index + 1}: ${line.trim().slice(0, 120)}`;
   843	      // Only a value token is deferred. An open question stays an error in
   844	      // every packet, because it names a decision nobody has made.
   845	      if (tokenGated && draftPacket && match[0] === '[YOUR_VALUE_HERE:' && !CLARIFICATION_MARKER_RE.test(line)) {
   846	        draftTokens.push(finding);
   847	        return;
   848	      }
   849	      findings.push(finding);
   850	    });
   851	  }
   852	  if (findings.length > 0) {
   853	    return entry('PLACEHOLDER_FILLED', 'error', `${findings.length} placeholder(s) found`, findings);
   854	  }
   855	  if (draftTokens.length > 0) {
   856	    return entry(
   857	      'PLACEHOLDER_FILLED',
   858	      'warn',

    13	    local value="$1"

    26	classify_status() {
    27	    local raw="${1:-}"
    28	    local normalized
    29	    normalized="$(speckit_status_trim "$raw")"
    30	
    31	    if [[ -z "$normalized" ]]; then
    32	        printf '%s\n' "unknown"
    33	        return 0
    34	    fi

    36	    # Cross-reference: strict-pass-freshness.ts's classifyStatus() (runtime/cli/sweep/strict-pass-freshness.ts)
    37	    # keeps a byte-equivalent complete/in-progress/planned word list. Update both when adding a status word.

    39	        printf '%s\n' "complete"
    40	        return 0
    41	    fi
    42	
    43	    # "implemented"/"implementing" also count as complete, but NOT when part of the
    44	    # "not implemented" / "not yet implemented" phrasing the planned bucket below

    48	       [[ ! "$normalized" =~ (^|[^[:alnum:]])not[[:space:]]+(yet[[:space:]]+)?(implemented|implementing)([^[:alnum:]]|$) ]]; then
    49	        printf '%s\n' "complete"
    50	        return 0
    51	    fi
    52	
    53	    # Negative phrases take precedence over words such as "started".

    56	        return 0
    57	    fi

    61	        printf '%s\n' "in-progress"
    62	        return 0
    63	    fi

   737	    const stamp = TEMPLATE_STAMP_RE.exec(line);
   738	    if (!stamp) continue;
   739	    const major = Number(stamp[1]);
   740	    const minor = Number(stamp[2]);
   741	    return major > TOKEN_GATE_MIN_MAJOR || (major === TOKEN_GATE_MIN_MAJOR && minor >= TOKEN_GATE_MIN_MINOR);
   742	  }
   743	  return false;
   744	}

   753	    .replace(/["']$/u, '')

   760	// The complete bucket of classify_status in status-classifier.sh, which keeps
   761	// the word list this must stay equal to.
   762	function statusIsComplete(normalized: string): boolean {
   763	  if (/(^|[^a-z0-9])(complete|completed|done|shipped|delivered|finished|closed)([^a-z0-9]|$)/u.test(normalized)) return true;
   764	  return /(^|[^a-z0-9])(implemented|implementing)([^a-z0-9]|$)/u.test(normalized)
   765	    && !/(^|[^a-z0-9])not\s+(yet\s+)?(implemented|implementing)([^a-z0-9]|$)/u.test(normalized);
   766	}

   768	// Reports whether spec.md's Status is exactly Draft. Mirrors the shell classifier:
   769	// quotes, case, trailing punctuation and repeated spaces do not change the
   770	// answer, any other word does. An older spec is read by its first Status row. A
   771	// v2.3 spec may carry more than one metadata table, and a Complete row in any of
   772	// them is a completion claim, so that row is the one read.
   773	function specStatusIsDraft(folder: string): boolean {
   774	  const spec = readIfExists(path.join(folder, 'spec.md'));
   775	  if (!spec) return false;
   776	  const values: string[] = [];
   777	  for (const line of spec.split(/\r?\n/u)) {
   778	    if (!/^\s*\|/u.test(line)) continue;
   779	    const cells = line.split('|');
   780	    if (cells.length < 3) continue;
   781	    if (cleanStatusCell(cells[1]).toLowerCase() !== 'status') continue;
   782	    values.push(normalizeStatusValue(cells[2]));
   783	  }
   784	  if (values.length === 0) return false;
   785	  const value = carriesTokenGateStamp(spec) ? (values.find(statusIsComplete) ?? values[0]) : values[0];
   786	  return value === 'draft';
   787	}

   796	function validatePlaceholders(folder: string, level: SpecKitLevel): ValidationEntry {
   797	  const findings: string[] = [];
   798	  const draftTokens: string[] = [];
   799	  const draftPacket = specStatusIsDraft(folder);
   800	  // A workflow loop owns the freeform docs and rewrites them whole at
   801	  // synthesis, so a scaffolded skeleton's markers are not an author's debt.
   802	  for (const docName of validationDocsForLevel(folder, level).filter((docName) => !FREEFORM_WORKFLOW_DOCS.has(docName))) {
   803	    const content = readIfExists(path.join(folder, docName));
   804	    if (!content) continue;
   805	    const tokenGated = carriesTokenGateStamp(content);
   806	    const lines = content.split(/\r?\n/u);
   807	    // Track fenced code blocks: a line starting with ``` toggles in_code and is
   808	    // itself skipped, matching check-placeholders.sh awk behavior.
   809	    let inCode = false;
   810	    lines.forEach((line, index) => {
   811	      if (tokenGated) {
   812	        // A v2.3 doc: a fence opens with ``` or ~~~ at any indent, a marker in
   813	        // inline code is an example, and every marker on the line counts.
   814	        if (TOKEN_GATE_FENCE_RE.test(line)) {
   815	          inCode = !inCode;
   816	          return;
   817	        }
   818	        if (inCode) return;
   819	        const visible = stripInlineCode(line);
   820	        const markers = [...visible.matchAll(PLACEHOLDER_MARKERS_ALL_RE)].map((found) => found[0]);
   821	        const title = TEMPLATE_TITLE_RE.test(visible);
   822	        if (markers.length === 0 && !title) return;
   823	        const finding = `${docName}:${index + 1}: ${line.trim().slice(0, 120)}`;
   824	        if (!title && draftPacket && markers.every((marker) => marker === '[YOUR_VALUE_HERE:')) {
   825	          draftTokens.push(finding);
   826	        } else {
   827	          findings.push(finding);
   828	        }
   829	        return;
   830	      }
   831	      if (/^\s*```/u.test(line)) {
   832	        inCode = !inCode;
   833	        return;
   834	      }
   835	      if (inCode) return;
   836	      const match = PLACEHOLDER_MARKER_RE.exec(line);
   837	      if (!match) return;
   838	      // Skip inline-backtick-wrapped markers: if the matched marker is
   839	      // immediately preceded by a backtick on this line, it is escaped content
   840	      // (parity with the shell rule's grep -v of backtick-wrapped cases).
   841	      if (match.index > 0 && line.charAt(match.index - 1) === '`') return;
   842	      const finding = `${docName}:${index + 1}: ${line.trim().slice(0, 120)}`;
   843	      // Only a value token is deferred. An open question stays an error in
   844	      // every packet, because it names a decision nobody has made.
   845	      if (tokenGated && draftPacket && match[0] === '[YOUR_VALUE_HERE:' && !CLARIFICATION_MARKER_RE.test(line)) {
   846	        draftTokens.push(finding);
   847	        return;
   848	      }
   849	      findings.push(finding);
   850	    });
   851	  }
   852	  if (findings.length > 0) {
   853	    return entry('PLACEHOLDER_FILLED', 'error', `${findings.length} placeholder(s) found`, findings);
   854	  }
   855	  if (draftTokens.length > 0) {
   856	    return entry(
   857	      'PLACEHOLDER_FILLED',
   858	      'warn',
   859	      `${draftTokens.length} unfilled value token(s) in a Draft packet. Fill each one before the status leaves Draft`,
   860	      draftTokens,

   542	function stripInlineCode(content: string): string {
   543	  return content
   544	    .split('\n')
   545	    .map((line) => {
   546	      let out = '';
   547	      let index = 0;
   548	      while (index < line.length) {
   549	        if (line[index] !== '`') {
   550	          out += line[index];
   551	          index += 1;
   552	          continue;
   553	        }
   554	        const open = index;
   555	        while (line[index] === '`') index += 1;
   556	        const runLength = index - open;
   557	        const delimiter = '`'.repeat(runLength);
   558	        let close = line.indexOf(delimiter, index);
   559	        while (close !== -1 && (line[close - 1] === '`' || line[close + runLength] === '`')) {
   560	          close = line.indexOf(delimiter, close + 1);
   561	        }
   562	        if (close === -1) {
   563	          out += line.slice(open, index);
   564	          continue;
   565	        }
   566	        const end = close + runLength;
   567	        out += line.slice(open, end).replace(/[^\n]/gu, ' ');
   568	        index = end;
   569	      }
   570	      return out;
   571	    })
   572	    .join('\n');
   573	}

     1	---
     2	title: "483 -- Level 1 packet authored from the card"
     3	description: "This scenario validates that a cli-devin deepseek-v4-1-flash-1017-max worker can scaffold and fill a Level 1 packet from the authoring card alone, with strict validation passing and no token left."

     7	
     8	# 483 -- Level 1 packet authored from the card
     9	
    10	## 1. OVERVIEW
    11	
    12	This scenario validates the card as an authoring instruction. It dispatches one cli-devin deepseek-v4-1-flash-1017-max worker with the card as its guidance and a throwaway track as its only write path. The worker scaffolds and fills a Level 1 packet. The operator then runs strict validation and counts the tokens left in the five documents the scaffold wrote, `goal.md` among them because the run passes `--with-goal`.
    13	
    14	### Why This Matters
    15	
    16	A card that reads well but cannot drive a finished packet is a brochure. This scenario is the end to end check: one model, one card, one strict pass and zero tokens left.
    17	
    18	---
    19	
    20	## 2. SCENARIO CONTRACT
    21	
    22	Operators dispatch one worker, then validate the packet it wrote.
    23	
    24	- Objective: Prove that a cli-devin deepseek-v4-1-flash-1017-max worker writes a Level 1 packet from the card, that strict validation prints `RESULT: PASSED`, and that the five scaffolded documents hold no value token or open question marker.
    25	- Playbook ID: 483.
    26	- Real user request: `Use the authoring card to write a complete Level 1 packet for a small feature, then prove it passes strict validation with nothing left to fill.`
    27	- Prompt: `Use the authoring card to write a complete Level 1 packet for a small feature, then prove it passes strict validation with nothing left to fill.`
    28	- Preconditions: A checkout with Node, bash and `rg` on PATH, the `devin` CLI on PATH with `devin auth status` printing `Logged in`, the operator's approval for `--permission-mode dangerous` on this run, and phase 5 closed so the card exists. The scenario needs network access and one cli-devin deepseek-v4-1-flash-1017-max run.
    29	- Expected execution process: Remove any earlier throwaway track, write the worker brief, record the checkout status, dispatch the worker with cli-devin, validate the packet it wrote, count the tokens left, check that the worker changed nothing outside the track, then remove the track, the scratch path and the pointer.
    30	- Expected signals: The worker returns a final reply and `devin` exits `0`. The packet holds `spec.md`. Strict validation prints `RESULT: PASSED`. The token count prints `0`. The containment check prints `escaped=0`. The track, the scratch path and the pointer are gone at the end.
    31	- Desired user-visible outcome: The operator sees a finished Level 1 packet that a strict run accepts, with no authoring hint left for a reader to fill.
    32	- Pass/fail: PASS if the worker returns a reply, strict validation prints `RESULT: PASSED`, the token count is `0`, the containment check prints `escaped=0` and cleanup prints `cleanup=ok`. FAIL if any of those checks fails.
    33	
    34	---
    35	
    36	## 3. TEST EXECUTION
    37	
    38	### Prompt
    39	
    40	```
    41	Use the authoring card to write a complete Level 1 packet for a small feature, then prove it passes strict validation with nothing left to fill.
    42	```
    43	
    44	### Commands
    45	
    46	Run steps 1 to 4 from the checkout root. Step 1 writes the scratch path to a fixed file, so each later step recovers it. Step 2 runs the `devin` CLI. This scenario spends one cli-devin deepseek-v4-1-flash-1017-max run.
    47	
    48	1. Clear the throwaway track and write the worker brief.
    49	
    50	```bash
    51	OUT="$(mktemp -d)"
    52	POINTER=specs/system-speckit/054-weak-model-spec-authoring/007-playbook-catalog-readme-alignment/scratch/verify/scenario-483-out.txt
    53	mkdir -p "$(dirname "$POINTER")"
    54	printf '%s\n' "$OUT" > "$POINTER"
    55	echo "out=$OUT"
    56	echo "pointer=$POINTER"
    57	rm -rf specs/zz-pb-card
    58	cat > "$OUT/brief.txt" <<'TXT'
    59	GATE 3 IS PRE-RESOLVED. DO NOT ASK THE DOCUMENTATION-SCOPE QUESTION.
    60	
    61	You are a non-interactive dispatched worker. AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 and
    62	SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0 are set in your environment, which this repository's AGENTS.md
    63	defines as the autonomous child-dispatch exemption: the spec-folder question is pre-resolved
    64	and MUST NOT be asked. No answer can reach you, because nobody is at a prompt.
    65	
    66	Your write authority is already bound. The spec folder you create and fill is:
    67	  specs/zz-pb-card/001-card-authoring
    68	
    69	ROLE: You are a documentation author. You read one card and write one Level 1 packet.
    70	
    71	ALLOWED WRITE PATHS:
    72	  specs/zz-pb-card/ and everything under it
    73	
    74	BANNED OPERATIONS: git commit, git push, git checkout, git switch, git branch, git reset, git stash, generate-context.js, /speckit:save, and any edit outside specs/zz-pb-card/. Do not edit recommend-level.sh. Do not edit anything under .skilled/.
    75	
    76	TASK:
    77	1. Read .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/references/workflows/spec-authoring-card.md completely.
    78	2. Run exactly: bash .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/create.sh --skip-branch --with-goal --level 1 --track zz-pb-card --short-name card-authoring --number 1 "Author a Level 1 packet from the card"
    79	3. Fill spec.md, plan.md, tasks.md, implementation-summary.md and goal.md. Describe this feature in the packet and do not build it: a --quiet flag for .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/recommend-level.sh that prints only the final recommended-level line. Say in implementation-summary.md that the packet is planned and not implemented.
    80	4. Run: bash .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/validate.sh specs/zz-pb-card/001-card-authoring --strict
    81	5. Fix what it reports and run it again, at most three times in all.
    82	
    83	RETURN exactly one line: the last RESULT line validate.sh printed.
    84	TXT
    85	echo "brief=$(wc -l < "$OUT/brief.txt") lines"
    86	GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=core.fsmonitor GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=false git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all > "$OUT/status-before.txt"
    87	echo "status_before=$(wc -l < "$OUT/status-before.txt" | tr -d ' ') lines"
    88	```
    89	
    90	2. Dispatch one worker with cli-devin.
    91	
    92	```bash
    93	OUT="$(cat specs/system-speckit/054-weak-model-spec-authoring/007-playbook-catalog-readme-alignment/scratch/verify/scenario-483-out.txt)"
    94	AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0 devin -p --model deepseek-v4-1-flash-1017-max --permission-mode dangerous -- "$(cat "$OUT/brief.txt")" </dev/null > "$OUT/reply.txt" 2> "$OUT/reply.err"
    95	echo "devin_exit=$?"
    96	tail -n 1 "$OUT/reply.txt"
    97	```
    98	
    99	3. Validate the packet, count the tokens left and check that nothing outside the track changed.
   100	
   101	```bash
   102	OUT="$(cat specs/system-speckit/054-weak-model-spec-authoring/007-playbook-catalog-readme-alignment/scratch/verify/scenario-483-out.txt)"
   103	P=specs/zz-pb-card/001-card-authoring
   104	test -f "$P/spec.md" && echo "packet=$P"
   105	bash .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/validate.sh "$P" --strict > "$OUT/val.txt" 2>&1
   106	echo "val_exit=$?"
   107	grep 'RESULT:' "$OUT/val.txt"
   108	rg -o --no-filename 'YOUR_VALUE_HERE:|NEEDS CLARIFICATION:' "$P/spec.md" "$P/plan.md" "$P/tasks.md" "$P/implementation-summary.md" "$P/goal.md" | wc -l | tr -d ' '
   109	GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=core.fsmonitor GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=false git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all > "$OUT/status-after.txt"
   110	comm -13 <(sort "$OUT/status-before.txt") <(sort "$OUT/status-after.txt") | grep -v '^.. specs/zz-pb-card/' > "$OUT/escaped.txt"
   111	echo "escaped=$(wc -l < "$OUT/escaped.txt" | tr -d ' ')"
   112	```
   113	
   114	The containment check compares status lines, so a path that was already dirty before step 1 and changed again goes unseen. Run the scenario in a clean worktree for an exact check.
   115	
   116	4. Remove the throwaway track, the scratch path and the pointer. Copy any evidence you keep out of the scratch path first, because this step deletes it.
   117	
   118	```bash
   119	POINTER=specs/system-speckit/054-weak-model-spec-authoring/007-playbook-catalog-readme-alignment/scratch/verify/scenario-483-out.txt
   120	OUT="$(cat "$POINTER")"
   121	rm -rf specs/zz-pb-card "$OUT" "$POINTER"
   122	test ! -d specs/zz-pb-card && test ! -e "$OUT" && test ! -e "$POINTER" && echo "cleanup=ok"
   123	```
   124	
   125	### Expected
   126	
   127	Step 1 prints `out=` followed by the scratch path, then `pointer=specs/system-speckit/054-weak-model-spec-authoring/007-playbook-catalog-readme-alignment/scratch/verify/scenario-483-out.txt`, then a brief line count above 20, then `status_before=` with a line count. Step 2 prints `devin_exit=0`, then the worker's last `RESULT` line, and leaves the reply file in the scratch path. Step 3 prints `packet=specs/zz-pb-card/001-card-authoring`, then `val_exit=0`, then `RESULT: PASSED`, then `0`, then `escaped=0`. Step 4 prints `cleanup=ok`.
   128	
   129	### Evidence
   130	
   131	- The `out=` line, the `pointer=` line and the brief line count from step 1.
   132	- The reply file in the scratch path from step 2 and the worker's last `RESULT` line, copied out before step 4.
   133	- The packet path, the validation exit code, the `RESULT` line, the token count and the `escaped=` line from step 3.
   134	- The `cleanup=ok` line from step 4.
   135	
   136	### Pass / Fail
   137	
   138	- **Pass**: The worker returns a reply, the packet exists, strict validation prints `RESULT: PASSED`, the token count is `0`, step 3 prints `escaped=0` and step 4 prints `cleanup=ok`.
   139	- **Fail**: The worker returns no reply, the packet is missing, strict validation fails, the token count is above zero, step 3 prints `escaped=` above zero, or step 4 does not print `cleanup=ok`.
   140	
   141	### Failure Triage
   142	
   143	An `escaped=` count above zero means the worker wrote outside its track, so record the FAIL with `$OUT/escaped.txt` and restore each path it names before any retry. A missing packet means the worker did not run the scaffold command, so read `$OUT/reply.txt` and `$OUT/reply.err` and check that `devin auth status` prints `Logged in` before retrying. A free-tier rate-limit reply is a retry and not a FAIL, so wait for the reset the message names and run step 2 again. A failed strict run means the packet is incomplete, so read `$OUT/val.txt` and name the rule. A token count above zero means the card did not drive a finished fill, so record the token lines in `$OUT/val.txt` before the next run. Remove `specs/zz-pb-card` before every retry.

   715	const contract = JSON.parse(process.argv[2]);

   752	    local contract_json="$1"

   754	const contract = JSON.parse(process.argv[2]);
   755	const docs = contract.lifecycleRequiredDocs?.afterImplementationStarts || [];
   756	const docRe = /^(?:[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]*\/)?[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]*\.md$/u;
   757	for (const doc of docs) {
   758	  if (typeof doc !== 'string' || !docRe.test(doc) || doc.includes('..')) {
   759	    console.error('Internal template contract included an invalid lifecycle document name');
   760	    process.exit(3);

   771	        return 1
   772	    fi

   785	        requested_lazy_addon_doc "$contract_json" "goal.md"

   113	copy_templates_batch() {
   114	    local docs="$1"
   115	    local dest_dir="$2"
   116	    local render_level="$3"
   117	    local base_templates_dir="$4"
   118	    local renderer
   119	    renderer="$(_inline_gate_renderer_path)"
   120	
   121	    local template_paths=()
   122	    local doc_names=()
   123	    local template_name template_path
   124	    while IFS= read -r template_name; do
   125	        [[ -z "$template_name" ]] && continue
   126	        if ! _validate_contract_doc_name "$template_name"; then
   127	            echo "Error: invalid template document name for Level $render_level" >&2
   128	            return 1
   129	        fi
   130	        template_path="$(_manifest_template_path "$template_name" "$render_level" "$base_templates_dir")"
   131	        if [[ ! -f "$template_path" ]]; then
   132	            echo "Error: required template document missing for Level $render_level: $template_name" >&2
   133	            return 1
   134	        fi
   135	        if ! _ensure_dest_within_dir "$dest_dir" "$dest_dir/$template_name"; then
   136	            echo "Error: template destination escapes target folder for Level $render_level" >&2
   137	            return 1
   138	        fi
   139	        template_paths+=("$template_path")
   140	        doc_names+=("$template_name")
   141	    done <<< "$docs"
   142	
   143	    if [[ ${#template_paths[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
   144	        return 0
   145	    fi
   146	
   147	    local renderer_exit=0
   148	    "$renderer" --level "$render_level" --out-dir "$dest_dir" "${template_paths[@]}" || renderer_exit=$?
   149	    if [[ $renderer_exit -ne 0 ]]; then
   150	        return $renderer_exit
   405	    node --import "$loader" --input-type=module - "$level" "$resolver" <<'NODE'
   406	import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
   407	
   408	const [level, resolverPath] = process.argv.slice(2);
   409	try {
   410	  const resolver = await import(pathToFileURL(resolverPath).href);
   411	  const contract = resolver.resolveLevelContract(level);
   412	  process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(resolver.serializeLevelContract(contract)));
   413	} catch (error) {
   414	  const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
   415	  console.error(message || `Internal template contract could not be resolved for Level ${level}`);
   416	  if (process.env.SPECKIT_VERBOSE_RESOLVER === '1' && error instanceof Error && error.stack) {
   417	    console.error(error.stack);
   418	  }
   419	  process.exit(3);
   420	}
   421	NODE
   422	}
   423	
   424	level_contract_docs_from_json() {
   425	    local contract_json="$1"
   426	    node - "$contract_json" <<'NODE'
   427	const contract = JSON.parse(process.argv[2]);
   428	const docRe = /^(?:[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]*\/)?[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]*\.md$/u;
   429	const docs = [...(contract.requiredCoreDocs || []), ...(contract.requiredAddonDocs || [])];
   430	if (docs.length === 0) {
   431	  console.error('Internal template contract did not include required documents');
   432	  process.exit(3);
   433	}
   434	for (const doc of docs) {
   435	  if (typeof doc !== 'string' || !docRe.test(doc) || doc.includes('..')) {
   436	    console.error('Internal template contract included an invalid document name');
   437	    process.exit(3);
   438	  }
   439	  process.stdout.write(`${doc}\n`);
   440	}
   441	NODE
   442	}

For an older packet its absence is advisory.

    53	## 2. CRITERIA
    54	<!-- FILL: Write one row per requirement. The Then clause names a command. GOOD: AC-001: When `--quiet` runs, Then `wc -l` prints 1. WEAK: The feature works. -->
    55	
    56	One row per criterion. `AC-ID` is stable once written: supersede a criterion, never renumber it.
    57	
    58	| AC-ID | REQ | Given / When / Then | Verification | Status | Waiver |
    59	|-------|-----|---------------------|--------------|--------|--------|
    60	| AC-001 | REQ-001 | Given [YOUR_VALUE_HERE: context], When [YOUR_VALUE_HERE: action], Then [YOUR_VALUE_HERE: observable outcome] | [YOUR_VALUE_HERE: command, file:line, or artifact that proves it] | Unmet | - |
    61	
    62	### Status values
    63	
    64	| Value | Meaning |
    65	|-------|---------|
    66	| `Met` | Verified. The Verification cell names evidence that was actually observed. |
    67	| `Unmet` | Not yet satisfied. Blocks closure. |
    68	| `Waived` | Deliberately not pursued. Requires an ADR in the Waiver cell. |
    69	| `Superseded` | Replaced by a different criterion or decision. Requires an ADR in the Waiver cell. |
    70	
    71	### Waiver cell
    72	
    73	Write `-` when the row is `Met` or `Unmet`. Write `ADR-NNN` when the row is
    74	`Waived` or `Superseded`, naming a decision record that exists in
    75	`decision-record.md`. A waiver naming an ADR that is not there fails validation:
    76	the point of a waiver is that someone recorded the reasoning, so an unbacked
    77	waiver is treated as an unmet criterion rather than as a pass.

   124	## 8. FILL EVERY TOKEN
   125	
   126	A scaffold stamped `v2.3` or later carries tokens. A token starts with `[YOUR_VALUE_HERE:` and ends at the next closing bracket. Replace the whole token, brackets included, with real content. Do not leave a token in a finished packet.
   127	
   128	If you cannot answer a question the token asks, write `UNKNOWN` in its place and write an open question in `goal.md` section 4.
   129	
   130	A token in a packet whose `spec.md` says `Status: Draft` is a warning, so strict validation can pass with tokens still in the file. A token in any other status is an error. Do not use the warning as permission. Count the tokens.

   319	    expect(result.category).toBe(CATEGORY.OVERSIZED_PHRASE);

   321	    expect(result.phrases[0].raw).toHaveLength(120);
   322	    expect(result.phrases[0].truncated).toBe(true);
   323	  });
   324	});
   325	
   326	// ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   327	// Corpus walk
   328	// ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   329	
   330	describe('walkCorpus', () => {
   331	  it('walks both roots, prunes excluded trees, and ignores non-markdown files', () => {
   332	    const root = makeTempDir('speckit-trigger-walk-');
   333	    writeDoc(root, 'specs/track/a.md', frontmatter(['a']));
   334	    writeDoc(root, 'specs/track/notes.txt', 'ignored');

   340	    writeDoc(root, '.skilled/skills/demo/node_modules/pkg/readme.md', frontmatter(['vendored']));
   341	
   342	    const { files } = walkCorpus(root, { roots: CORPUS_ROOTS });
   343

   347	      'specs/track/research/synthesis.md',
   348	    ]);
   349	  });
   350	
   351	  // CI rebuilds the committed index from a fresh checkout, so an ignored file a
   352	  // working checkout happens to hold must not change what a local build indexes.
   353	  it('skips what git ignores, keeps a tracked file that matches an ignore rule, and lists neither as skipped', () => {
   354	    const root = makeTempDir('speckit-trigger-gitignore-');
   355	    spawnSync('git', ['init', '--quiet'], { cwd: root });
   356	    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(root, '.gitignore'), 'specs/**/containment/\nspecs/track/local.md\nspecs/track/forced.md\n');
   357	    writeDoc(root, 'specs/track/a.md', frontmatter(['a']));
   358	    writeDoc(root, 'specs/track/local.md', frontmatter(['local only']));
   359	    writeDoc(root, 'specs/track/review/containment/copy/spec.md', frontmatter(['containment copy']));
   360	    writeDoc(root, 'specs/track/forced.md', frontmatter(['tracked anyway']));
   361	    spawnSync('git', ['add', '--force', 'specs/track/forced.md'], { cwd: root });
   362	
   363	    const { files, skipped } = walkCorpus(root, { roots: CORPUS_ROOTS });
   364	
   365	    expect(files).toEqual(['specs/track/a.md', 'specs/track/forced.md']);
   366	    expect(skipped.filter((entry) => entry.path.startsWith('specs/'))).toEqual([]);
   367	  });
   368	
   369	  it('refuses a symlinked document whose target is outside the repository', () => {
   370	    const root = makeTempDir('speckit-trigger-outside-');
   371	    const outside = makeTempDir('speckit-trigger-external-');
   372	    fs.mkdirSync(path.join(root, 'specs/track'), { recursive: true });
   373	    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(root, 'specs/track/a.md'), '---\ntitle: a\ntrigger_phrases:\n  - "inside phrase"\n---\n# a\n');
   374	    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(outside, 'secret.md'), '---\ntitle: s\ntrigger_phrases:\n  - "external phrase"\n---\n# s\n');
   375	    fs.symlinkSync(path.join(outside, 'secret.md'), path.join(root, 'specs/track/leak.md'), 'file');
   376	
   377	    const { files, skipped } = walkCorpus(root, { roots: CORPUS_ROOTS });
   378	
   379	    expect(files).toEqual(['specs/track/a.md']);
   380	    expect(skipped).toContainEqual({ path: 'specs/track/leak.md', reason: 'symlink target outside the repository' });
